default.law: European Accessibility Act (Directive (EU) 2019/882), as transposed into national law
default.fine: penalties set by each member state (in Germany up to €100,000)

t.none: The scan found no automatically detectable violations on the checked pages. That is a good sign — but only part of the requirements can be tested automatically (see the self-check).
t.statement_found: The home page links to what looks like accessibility information. Check that it covers everything the EAA asks for (Annex V) — the template below helps you compare.
t.statement_missing: No link to accessibility information was found on the home page. The EAA asks for it in your general terms or an equivalent document — if it sits inside your terms, make sure it is easy to find; otherwise add a page and link it, e.g. from the footer. A template is included below.
t.self_intro: Automated tests catch only part of the barriers. These three checks take about twenty minutes together:
t.template_intro: The EAA asks service providers to publish this information in their general terms or an equivalent document (Annex V); national laws may ask for more. Fill in the {PLACEHOLDERS}, delete what does not apply. A working aid, not legal advice.
t.frame: This automated check is the kind of first pass a market-surveillance authority typically starts with (automated testing plus formal duties) — fully automatic and free. It is not a conformity certificate and not legal advice. Legal frame: {law}; {fine}. Full conformity also needs an expert evaluation against EN 301 549.
t.footer: free · not a certificate, not legal advice · This report is deleted after 30 days.
t.auto2_intro: Checks that used to need a person, now run by our robot on your pages. They do not click or submit anything.
t.reflow_ok: At phone width (320 CSS px) all checked pages fit without sideways scrolling.
t.reflow_bad: At 320 CSS px wide these pages need sideways scrolling ({pages}) — WCAG 1.4.10 asks that content reflows. Elements sticking out:
t.kb_reach: We pressed Tab {stops} times and reached {reached} different elements.
t.kb_trap: Focus seems stuck: the last Tab presses cycle between {items} — keyboard users may not get past this point (WCAG 2.1.2).
t.kb_invisible: On {n} stop(s) we could not detect any visible change when the element got focus (WCAG 2.4.7). Please tab through these yourself — sometimes the focus style is drawn in a way we cannot see:
t.kb_hidden: On {n} stop(s) focus landed on something that is not visible on screen (for example a closed menu) — keyboard users lose track of where they are:
t.kb_ok: Every stop showed a visible change, no traps.
t.sr_none: We did not find a product page to check automatically.
t.sr_unavailable: The product page did not give our robot a readable page (often a bot check) — please test it yourself.
t.sr_unnamed: {n} button(s) on the page have no name — a screen reader just says “button”.
t.fb_ok: A way to report barriers is there: {how}.
t.fb_bad: The accessibility statement gives no email address or contact form for reporting barriers.
t.fb_unchecked: No statement found, so there is nothing to check yet — the template below includes this section.
t.lead_excellent: Your shop is in great shape — only details are left. Well done.
t.lead_strong: Most of it already works. Below: what is good, then the few things left to fix.
t.lead_good: A solid base. Below: what already works, then what to fix — most important first.
t.lead_grow: The basics are within reach. Below: what already works, then the fixes — most important first.

t.fwd_wa_text: Accessibility check for {host} ({law}): {p} of {n} checks passed. What is left to fix: {url}

rules.color-contrast: Text has too little contrast against its background, so people with low vision cannot read it. Fix: adjust the colours until the contrast ratio is at least 4.5:1 (normal text) or 3:1 (large text).
rules.image-alt: Images without alternative text — a screen reader can only read out the file name. Fix: a meaningful alt attribute for images that carry content, an empty alt="" for purely decorative ones.
rules.link-name: Links without an accessible name (for example icon-only links). Fix: add link text or an aria-label that describes the destination.
rules.button-name: Buttons without an accessible name — screen-reader users only hear “button”. Fix: add visible text or an aria-label.
rules.label: Form fields without a linked label. Fix: a <label for=…> or aria-label for each field.
rules.html-has-lang: The document does not declare its language, so screen readers pick the wrong pronunciation. Fix: <html lang="en"> (or your shop's language).
rules.html-lang-valid: Invalid language code in the lang attribute. Fix: use a valid code (e.g. "en", "de").
rules.document-title: Page without a meaningful title. Fix: a distinct <title> on every page.
rules.duplicate-id: Duplicate IDs in the HTML — assistive technology can mix elements up. Fix: make IDs unique.
rules.landmark-one-main: No <main> landmark — screen-reader users cannot jump straight to the content. Fix: wrap the main content in <main>.
rules.region: Content outside landmark regions. Fix: structure content with <header>/<nav>/<main>/<footer>.
rules.page-has-heading-one: No H1 heading. Fix: exactly one H1 per page that names its content.
rules.heading-order: The heading hierarchy skips levels (e.g. H2 → H4). Fix: nest levels without gaps.
rules.aria-allowed-attr: ARIA attributes that are not allowed on this element. Fix: remove the attribute or correct the element's role.
rules.aria-required-attr: ARIA role without its required attributes. Fix: add the missing aria attributes.
rules.aria-valid-attr-value: ARIA attribute points to an ID that does not exist. Fix: correct the reference.
rules.aria-hidden-focus: Focusable elements inside aria-hidden areas — keyboard users land on “nothing”. Fix: tabindex="-1" or change the structure.
rules.select-name: Select box without an accessible name. Fix: link a label.
rules.frame-title: iframe without a title. Fix: set a descriptive title.
rules.meta-viewport: Zoom is disabled by the viewport meta tag. Fix: remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale.
rules.list: List markup is broken (children outside <li>). Fix: correct the list structure.
rules.listitem: <li> outside a list. Fix: wrap it in <ul>/<ol>.
rules.tabindex: Positive tabindex values scramble the focus order. Fix: remove tabindex > 0 and rely on the natural DOM order.
rules.nested-interactive: Interactive elements nested inside each other (a button inside a link, etc.). Fix: un-nest them.
rules.image-redundant-alt: Alt text repeats the text right next to the image. Fix: empty the alt or make it different.

self_checks: Buy all the way with the keyboard

Our robot tabs through your home page but never buys anything. Do it yourself with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space: product → cart → checkout, up to the payment step. Can you choose a size, open and close every dialog, and reach the “pay” button?
Submit the checkout form half-filled on purpose. Does each field say in words what is missing — or is it only marked red?
Mac: VoiceOver with Cmd+F5; Windows: NVDA (free). Listen to one product page from top to bottom: does it make sense without seeing it — images described, options understandable?

good.structure: Screen readers can jump straight to the content
good.focus_order: The keyboard order is not scrambled
good.nesting: No controls hidden inside other controls
good.reflow: Works at phone width without sideways scrolling
good.keyboard: Keyboard focus never gets stuck or lost
good.statement: Accessibility information is linked from the home page
good.feedback: There is a way to report barriers
good.screen_reader: A screen reader announces name, price and buy button
